correctness.rationale: The original scientific text stated n>=1, but at n=1 the source writes distinct first-intermediate B_1 and terminal B_n equations for the same variable, without specifying a single ODE. The final supplied RESULT.md expressly restricts to n>=2 (the first unambiguous model domain). For every such n, the weighted quantity Q=B0+sum alpha^-i B_i +alpha^-n P has Qdot=-d(B0+sum alpha^-i B_i)<=0, and N+H+G has dissipative bound. Scalar variation of constants forces H,G, B0 and all B_i positive for every t>0, then Pdot=kappa B_n>0 and V(t)<=V(t0)exp[-mu P(t0)(t-t0)] for t>=t0>0. This proves global existence and V->0; it does not claim a uniform rate or the unspecific n=1 model.
